Subject: Follow-up: Redwood demo recap and proposed next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next actions so nothing falls through the cracks:

1) What we demoed: Redwood inference runtime (low-latency text generation), per-route cost breakdowns, and the Optimize suggestions for quantization/batching that reduce per-token spend.

2) Decision criteria you mentioned: predictable unit economics, SOC2 + DPA, and an integration path that doesn't require re-architecting existing inference pipelines.

3) Immediate asks from your side: confirmation of the economic/budget owner and procurement contact, and an expected timeline or budget window (you mentioned Q4).

Next steps I propose: I’ll send a short mutual action plan + two pricing scenarios (pilot and first-year committed) and a compliance packet. If you can introduce the budget owner and procurement, we’ll tailor the pricing/contract to their needs.

I attached a one-page mutual action plan (Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf) and will follow with detailed pricing. Can you confirm who owns the budget (name & email) and whether procurement prefers PO or contract-first?

Quick 30-min options for next week if useful: Tue 10–10:30am PT / Wed 1–1:30pm PT.

Thanks,

Procurement typically requests a short scoping doc + initial T&Cs before engaging legal. I’ve attached our internal scoping notes for context. Please share a pricing workbook and the compliance pack.

- Attachment: pricing-scenarios.xlsx (pilot vs committed-year layouts)
- Attachment: Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan) — we’ll update after alignment call
- Compliance packet link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodMAP

Quick bullets to help with internal triage:
- Pilot profile: 3 months, up to 200M tokens/mo peak, single-region (us-west) deployment
- Target SLAs: 99.9% uptime for API, P95 latency < 250ms for short prompts
- Data controls: optional VPC/private deployment, customer-managed KMS available

Questions for you to flag to the team:
1) Who owns the procurement/commercial conversation (name + email)?
2) Target budget band for pilot and whether budget is already allocated or requires reforecasting
3) Any mandatory contractual clauses (e.g., specific insurance levels, export controls) beyond the standard DPA

If it helps, I can put together a 30-min walkthrough for Elena + procurement next Thu/Fri — proposed slots: Thu 7/15 10–10:30am PT or Fri 7/16 11–11:30am PT.

Hello Priya — procurement here. Thanks for the materials. To move to commercial review we need the following items delivered in a single package:

1) SOC2 Type II report (latest)
2) Current DPA and standard contract terms (or a statement of willingness to sign our DPA)
3) List of subprocessors + geographic data residency commitments
4) Details on KMS options and any encryption-at-rest/export controls
5) Insurance certificates (cyber liability) and export compliance affirmations
6) An initial commercial contact for redlines (name/email) — we prefer a commercial lead rather than AE for contract negotiations

Please upload the package to our procurement portal or send a secured Drive link. We also require a signed NDA before we share non-public worksheets — here is our DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/medicore-nda

Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx

Once we have the items above we’ll open a contract ticket (PO vs. standard master services agreement) and share an estimated internal review timeline (typically 7–10 business days).

Regards,
MediCore Procurement Ops
procure@medicore.com
